parsed.rationale: Sinus rhythm with narrow QRS and high precordial voltage (deep S in V2 of about 25 mm plus tall R in V4–V5, so S V2 + R V5 is over 35 mm); the 2–3 mm concave ST elevation with large T waves in V2–V3 fits LVH or early repolarization rather than an infarct, because there are no reciprocal changes or Q waves, although hyperacute anterior T waves cannot be fully excluded from the image alone.
